title: Crimson Desert wins 'PC Game of the Year' at the 2026 Golden Joystick Awards
summary: Resident Evil Requiem and Meccha Chameleon were the night's other big winners.
body: There was some fun conversation here at PC Gamer recently about the anachronistic name of The Golden Joystick Awards. Who even uses a joystick anymore? Flight sim diehards, fighting game enthusiasts, and not many others. So why is it called that? Joysticks , really? Simply put, the name reflects the age of the awards, which debuted in 1983, making it the longest-running publicly-voted videogame awards show of all time, according to Wikipedia. Back in those days, joysticks were it, and trust me, they weren't the sweet pieces of hardware we have access to now. But we loved 'em! And we used them to play games like the Golden Joysticks' first-ever game of the year, Jetpac. It was a banger! Here we are, 43 years later, and much has changed: From a tiny ceremony handing out five trophies, the Golden Joysticks have grown to become one of the biggest videogame awards events of the year, watched by millions of people around the world on just about every streaming platform you can name. Yet that name, the Golden Joystick Awards , remains. Frankly, I'm glad about that. A little bit of reliability in this world is good for everyone.
